title: Open-weight benchmark via real fan-out model buckets (Kimi K3 / GLM 5.2 vs Anthropic / GPT)
body: SPEC'D 2026-07-23 (reframed by Andrew: piggyback on real in-flight Workflow fan-outs, NOT a standalone matrix). Split fan-out agents into 3 buckets on the IDENTICAL subtask -> judge scores all 3 -> append quality/cost/speed to conversations/openweight-scoreboard.jsonl. Buckets: Anthropic (model:sonnet/fable, flat Max), GPT (agentType:codex, flat Codex sub), open-weight (headless `claude -p` via translation proxy -> OpenRouter, pay-per-token, NEVER touches Max). VERIFIED (Context7/CC source): Claude Code speaks only Anthropic /v1/messages; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL must be Anthropic-compatible; OpenRouter is OpenAI-format so needs a proxy (LiteLLM or claude-code-router); env is per-process so open-weight terminal never uses the sub; Workflow model override is Anthropic-only so open-weight bucket MUST shell out. SHARES INFRA with idea_2 (proxy + OPENROUTER_API_KEY dotfile + `ow-run` wrapper = idea_2's launcher in headless form) — build once. ACCEPTANCE (see spec): (1) ow-run completes from glm-5.2 AND kimi-k3 via proxy w/ token+wallclock; (2) prove OpenRouter charge + zero Anthropic-sub delta; (3) 3-bucket harness runs in ONE real fan-out, appends 3 rows; (4) judge scores all 3 + eyes-on open-weight render; (5) >=N datapoints/bucket before ANY routing-ladder edit; (6) non-goals held. OpenRouter key wired 2026-07-23; AC1 GREEN (ow-run smoke-tested both models: GLM 5.2 $0.0012/4.66s vs Kimi K3 $0.0061/11.74s, equal quality — GLM 5x cheaper/2.5x faster). JUDGED 2026-07-23 prioritization-judge: 24/30 PROCEED-IF-CAPACITY (0 block, 1 warn EVID-measured-not-assumed: $-payoff unproven until >=N datapoints). NOTE: routing/infra meta-item — NOT for build-next auto-pick (that loop skips routing-self items); Andrew-driven, rides on real fan-outs. Spec: conversations/2026-07-23-openweight-benchmark-spec.md

Report + judge score to follow this session. title: Grab: live optimistic DOM move preview (DevTools-style drag) backed by real source edits
detail: DevTools can drag a div live via CDP DOM.moveTo but the move is ephemeral. Raven overlay runs in-page so insertBefore gives the same instant canvas feel with no CDP: drag in Layers tree (or directly on canvas) -> element moves immediately as optimistic preview -> pending-changes tray holds the source-edit intent -> agent applies, reconcile via existing domSnapshotHash machinery; discard restores. Extends the existing style-edit live-preview pattern to structure. Hazards: framework re-render replacing moved node mid-drag (detached-row guards exist), drop-target ambiguity (insertion markers like DevTools).

title: Portrait transforms on scroll into a rear-view time regression through every workstation Andrew has worked at
detail: The portfolio portrait becomes, as you scroll, a rear view of Andrew looking at his computer -- and each further scroll step regresses to an earlier workstation. Andrew's stated sequence (present -> past): current workstation -> 3600 Fillmore Street -> Beach Street -> Webster or Bush Street -> [maybe Santa Barbara, Andrew flagged as 'kinda weird', probably cut] -> North Carolina barracks room (definite) -> Corte Madera, on his parents' computer (definite). The arc: the career told as the rooms it happened in, ending at a kid on a family machine. Same camera position each time -- over-the-shoulder, screen-lit -- so the room changes and the posture does not. OPEN: source imagery. Either find real photos of those rooms, or interview Andrew for vivid per-room detail (what the camera sees: desk, monitor count, wall, window, light, era-correct machine) and generate. Andrew explicitly asked to be interviewed for this if photos don't exist. NOT started -- he deferred it to 2026-07-26 and asked to be reminded.

title: Grab: drop a PNG onto the canvas and free-position it (position:absolute drag)
detail: Drag an image file from Finder onto the live overlay canvas -> it lands as a new absolutely-positioned element at the drop point -> drag it around freely to place it -> the pending-changes tray carries BOTH the asset (copy the file into the repo, e.g. public/) and the source edit (new img/div with the resolved position). Distinct from idea_grab_live_move_preview, which moves EXISTING nodes: this ADDS a node and a binary asset, which the change model has never carried. Two new capabilities needed: (1) an asset channel in the grab payload -- today changes are style/structure intent, nothing carries a file; (2) free x/y positioning, where today all dragging is layers-tree reorder. Use cases: dropping a Figma export in as a design-comp overlay to eyeball against, and genuinely placing an image into the page. Those two want different outputs -- a throwaway comp overlay should NOT emit a source edit -- so the mode is a real design question, not a detail. Also unresolved: what position:absolute is relative to (nearest positioned ancestor vs a new wrapper), and whether px offsets are an acceptable thing for Raven to write given it argues for tokens and flow layout.

Stop-hook race: design-judge-gate.sh and auto-save-on-turn.sh run in parallel on Stop; auto-save stages everything and commits without pathspecs while the gate may be rejecting the turn. Pre-existing (not introduced by 2026-07-26 enforcement rebuild); flagged by Sol adverse pass. Fix options: serialize via one wrapper script, or make auto-save honor the gate's exit state.

Provenance/scope harness as a mechanical gate. Two repeat verification failures in the NC-cleanup session: (1) sweep scope narrower than claim scope (grep covered src/ only, the written claim said repo-wide) — a REPEAT of the promoted source-of-truth-diff-covers-SCOPE rule, so per the recurrence rule it needs a mechanical trigger, not more prose; (2) provenance rewrites must be overlap-checked against every replaced text, not just the headline file (first rewrite carried 4-10-word runs, caught by the Sol pass). Candidate: raven audit_content provenance mode (longest-common-word-run vs a named predecessor/source) plus a claim-scope check that widens any 'X is gone' grep to the whole repo before the claim is written.

Browse-and-pick pattern discovery from a shared corpus — the Mobbin/Clicky half of the pattern library that is still missing. Andrew's use case, verbatim: 'I wanted examples of a scrolling mouse icon in a hero image from around the web, and I wish Raven would show me some, then I could have chosen one and it would then implement for me.' Today search_references only searches what THIS user already captured with capture_reference (grab-based, one site at a time), map_reference_to_tokens translates values onto the project's tokens but writes no code, and the tool that would have written code (compose_build_prompt) was deleted in the §13 pre-gate round 5. So all three legs of his ask are missing: (a) a seeded/shared corpus of real-world patterns searchable by INTENT ('scroll cue in a hero'), not just by host/tag/note over your own captures; (b) a visual pick step — search_references returns JSON records and never images, so there is nothing to choose FROM; (c) a hand-off that actually implements the chosen pattern in the user's tokens/framework. Team-lens angle: a shared corpus is a per-org asset and a natural Morven paid surface; free tier keeps the solo capture-your-own path. Open questions: corpus sourcing and licensing/attribution for third-party captures, whether the pick step ships as thumbnails in the MCP response or a Grab-style local surface, and whether implementation returns code or a build prompt (the deleted-tool question, reopened by a real use case).

Overlay panel scroll preservation across renders. Reported by Andrew 2026-08-06, verbatim: 'as I have been using the panels sometimes I click in to change a value and the panel resets scrolling back to the top instead of just letting me use the input to change whatever I am trying to change.' Mechanism: renderPanel() rewrites panel.innerHTML / panelLeft.innerHTML wholesale, destroying the .raven-grab-body scroll container and rebuilding it at scrollTop 0. 81 renderPanel() call sites; only expandLayerDuringDrag preserved scroll. Many renders are background (pollBatch, pollLayerOperation, dispatch lifecycle), which is why it read as intermittent. Fixed in-tree: renderPanel captures and restores each panel's scrollTop, gated on a content-identity key (panel A = selectedElement + activeTabA + editScope; panel B = activeTabB) so a genuinely different list still starts at the top. Regression test test/grab-overlay-scroll-preservation.test.mjs (real Chromium), both directions falsifiable by mutant. NOT yet verified on Andrew's own surface.

Reference-site list for the browse-and-pick corpus (companion to the 2026-08-05 P1 entry). Andrew has now named three inspiration galleries as the shape to match: clickyhq.com, mobbin.com, and — added 2026-08-06, verbatim: 'motion.ai is a nother inspiration site etc' — motion.ai (bare curl returns 403 behind bot protection, so it exists but was not rendered; the name is recorded as he wrote it and not disambiguated against motion.dev / motion.page). The 'etc' says the list is open, so treat it as a growing set rather than three fixed sources. Motion-specific angle worth noting: a motion gallery implies the corpus needs to carry INTERACTION and animation exemplars, not just static screens — which is exactly the interaction axis spec-pattern-library.md §4 calls the only genuinely new taxonomy axis, and it is the axis a screenshot corpus cannot represent. Does NOT change the §5/§14 legal position: scraping any of these is still a non-goal and a stored corpus of third-party captures is still blocked on Andrew's legal call.

Voice input for every overlay text field, starting with the Instructions box. Andrew, verbatim: 'Anytime we have any sort of input, we should be able to have voice. So I think it's key that we get voice to the instructions box so that that transmits over to the coding agent.' Shape: mic affordance on the Instructions textarea (and generalized to overlay inputs), Web Speech API in Chrome, transcript lands in the field and rides the existing selection payload to the agent. Overlay file browser/raven-grab.js + byte-identical mirror web/public/raven-grab.js; testability via injected fake SpeechRecognition since headless Chromium has no live recognizer.

Mood boards as a Taste Engine output. Andrew, verbatim: 'create mood boards based on the taste engine. So when you do initial taste interview, get a mood board going. Also, it can ask users to make a mood board and show an example to try and, like, get their thinking.' Two directions: (a) generate a mood board FROM interview answers (references question already takes examples; pattern-library thumbnails are ready-made tiles), (b) elicit one from the user with a shown example as a calibration aid during get_taste_interview.

Higgsfield brand-to-design-system onboarding flow. Andrew saw a video using Higgsfield to create a brand, then importing design systems into Claude Code; he will share the YouTube link and wants it incorporated. His framing, verbatim: 'the design system is the core piece upfront that we have to make to start off on the right foot, and that should be one of the outputs of the taste engine.' BLOCKED on the link; when it arrives, watch it and spec how a Higgsfield-generated brand feeds generate_design_system / DESIGN.md.

Drag-and-drop 'things on the screen' while using the Raven design panels — Andrew reports it not working for him 2026-08-06, verbatim: 'I thought we already did this, but it wasn't working for me yesterday... if that means opening a full page overlay or opening a new tab... some other kind of bridge, let's figure that out.' Live evidence gathered 2026-08-07 on a real proxied session (lusion.co, Chrome): panel drag-by-header WORKS, Layers row drag-to-reorder WORKS (queued Move pending + live page preview). So either his surface/browser differs or he means direct on-canvas element dragging, which does not exist today. ANSWERED 2026-08-07: Andrew picked 'Dragging elements on the page itself' — direct manipulation of actual page content, a NEW FEATURE, not a repro. This is idea_grab_live_move_preview (captured 2026-07-24) promoted to a confirmed ask: drag on canvas -> optimistic insertBefore preview -> pending-changes tray -> agent applies. Build after voice input lands (same file, serialize).

Higgsfield-to-design-system flow: accept local image files as taste references with palette/trait extraction; brand-kit hex -> token importer feeding generate_design_system; document the Higgsfield MCP -> mood board -> generate_design_system flow as a skill/docs page; optionally slot Higgsfield behind create_generation_job later
